docs.title: How to Read This Table Format
docs.text:
Har function/method is table format mein explain hoga:

Field Matlab Purpose Ye kya karta hai (simple English/Urdu mein) Syntax General likhne ka tareeqa Example Real code Output Code chalane se kya milega When to use Kab use karna hai Common Mistakes Beginners jo galti karte hain

docs.title: 1. Strings
docs.text: Strings text data hoti hai jaise "Hello World". Python mein strings immutable hoti hain (ek baar ban gayi to change nahi ho sakti, naya string banta hai).

docs.title: strip()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String ke shuru aur akhir se extra spaces (ya specified characters) hata deta hai Syntax string.strip(chars=None) Example " hello ".strip() Output 'hello' When to use User input clean karne ke liye, ya file se aaye data ke extra whitespace hatane ke liye Common Mistakes Beginners sochte hain ye string ke beech ke spaces bhi hata deta hai — nahi, sirf shuru aur akhir ke 
text = "   Hello World   "
print(text.strip())        # 'Hello World'
print("xxHelloxx".strip("x"))  # 'Hello'

docs.title: lstrip()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Sirf left side (shuru) se spaces/characters hatata hai Syntax string.lstrip(chars=None) Example " hello".lstrip() Output 'hello' When to use Jab sirf left side clean karna ho Common Mistakes rstrip() se confuse ho jaate hain (l = left, r = right) 
print("   Hello".lstrip())  # 'Hello'

docs.title: rstrip()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Sirf right side (akhir) se spaces/characters hatata hai Syntax string.rstrip(chars=None) Example "hello ".rstrip() Output 'hello' When to use File lines ke akhir se newline \n hatane ke liye common hai Common Mistakes lstrip() ke saath mix up 
line = "Hello World\n"
print(line.rstrip())  # 'Hello World'

docs.title: split()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String ko break karke list bana deta hai, kisi separator ke basis par Syntax string.split(separator=None, maxsplit=-1) Example "a,b,c".split(",") Output ['a', 'b', 'c'] When to use CSV data parse karne, sentence ko words mein todne ke liye Common Mistakes Bina argument diye .split() space se split karta hai — log bhool jaate hain default comma nahi hai 
sentence = "Python is fun"
print(sentence.split())          # ['Python', 'is', 'fun']
print("a,b,c".split(","))        # ['a', 'b', 'c']
print("a,b,c".split(",", 1))     # ['a', 'b,c']  -> maxsplit=1

docs.title: join()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List of strings ko ek single string bana deta hai (opposite of split) Syntax separator.join(iterable) Example ",".join(["a","b","c"]) Output 'a,b,c' When to use List ko CSV ya sentence banane ke liye Common Mistakes join() string par call hota hai, list par nahi — beginners list.join() likhne ki koshish karte hain jo galat hai 
words = ["Python", "is", "fun"]
print(" ".join(words))   # 'Python is fun'

docs.title: replace()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String ke andar ek text ko doosre text se replace karta hai Syntax string.replace(old, new, count=-1) Example "I like cats".replace("cats", "dogs") Output 'I like dogs' When to use Text cleaning, censoring, data formatting Common Mistakes Original string change nahi hoti (immutable) — naya assign karna zaroori hai 
s = "I like cats"
new_s = s.replace("cats", "dogs")
print(new_s)  # 'I like dogs'
print(s)      # 'I like cats' (original same rehta hai)

docs.title: find()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Substring ki position (index) return karta hai, nahi milne par -1 Syntax string.find(substring) Example "hello world".find("world") Output 6 When to use Jab pata karna ho ke koi word maujood hai ya nahi, bina error ke Common Mistakes index() se confuse karte hain — find() error nahi deta, -1 deta hai 
print("hello world".find("world"))  # 6
print("hello world".find("xyz"))    # -1

docs.title: index()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Substring ki position return karta hai, nahi milne par error deta hai Syntax string.index(substring) Example "hello".index("l") Output 2 When to use Jab confirm ho ke substring maujood hai Common Mistakes Agar substring na mile to ValueError crash ho jata hai — find() use karna safer hai jab uncertain ho 
print("hello".index("l"))  # 2
# "hello".index("z")  -> ValueError: substring not found

docs.title: startswith()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai string kisi particular text se start hoti hai ya nahi Syntax string.startswith(prefix) Example "hello.py".startswith("hello") Output True When to use File extensions check karna, URL prefix check karna (jaise "https://") Common Mistakes Case-sensitive hota hai — "Hello".startswith("hello") False hoga 
filename = "report.pdf"
print(filename.startswith("report"))  # True
url = "https://example.com"
print(url.startswith("https://"))     # True

docs.title: endswith()
lower()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Poori string ko lowercase mein convert karta hai Syntax string.lower() Example "HELLO".lower() Output 'hello' When to use Case-insensitive comparison ke liye (jaise email match karna) Common Mistakes Original string change nahi hoti 
print("HELLO World".lower())  # 'hello world'

docs.title: upper()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Poori string ko uppercase mein convert karta hai Syntax string.upper() Example "hello".upper() Output 'HELLO' When to use Headings, alerts, ya standardized codes (jaise country codes) Common Mistakes Numbers/symbols par koi effect nahi hota 
print("hello123".upper())  # 'HELLO123'

docs.title: title()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Har word ka pehla letter capital kar deta hai Syntax string.title() Example "hello world".title() Output 'Hello World' When to use Names, headings display karne ke liye Common Mistakes Apostrophes ke saath ajeeb result deta hai: "it's".title() -> "It'S" 
print("hello world".title())  # 'Hello World'

docs.title: capitalize()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Sirf pehle letter ko capital karta hai, baaki sab lowercase Syntax string.capitalize() Example "hello WORLD".capitalize() Output 'Hello world' When to use Sentences ko properly format karne ke liye Common Mistakes title() se confuse hote hain — capitalize() sirf ek word capitalize karta hai (sentence ka pehla) 
print("hello WORLD".capitalize())  # 'Hello world'

docs.title: casefold()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose lower() jaisa hi hai lekin zyada aggressive — special/unicode characters ke liye better Syntax string.casefold() Example "ß".casefold() Output 'ss' When to use International text comparison ke liye (German jaisi languages) Common Mistakes Beginners lower() hi use karte rehte hain, casefold ke baare mein pata nahi hota 
print("Straße".casefold())  # 'strasse'
print("Straße".lower())     # 'straße'  (different!)

docs.title: swapcase()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Upper ko lower aur lower ko upper kar deta hai Syntax string.swapcase() Example "Hello World".swapcase() Output 'hELLO wORLD' When to use Kam use hota hai real projects mein, kabhi kabhi fun/text transformation ke liye Common Mistakes Real-world use rare hai — interview mein trick question ke liye pucha ja sakta hai 
print("Hello World".swapcase())  # 'hELLO wORLD'

docs.title: count()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String mein koi substring kitni baar aata hai, wo ginta hai Syntax string.count(substring) Example "banana".count("a") Output 3 When to use Word frequency check karne ke liye Common Mistakes Overlapping matches nahi ginta (jaise "aaaa".count("aa") -> 2, not 3) 
print("banana".count("a"))  # 3
print("aaaa".count("aa"))   # 2 (overlap count nahi hota)

docs.title: format()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String ke andar values insert karta hai (placeholders {} use karke) Syntax "text {}".format(value) Example "My name is {}".format("Ali") Output 'My name is Ali' When to use Dynamic strings banane ke liye (f-strings se pehle ye common tha) Common Mistakes Index numbers galat order mein dena: "{1} {0}".format("a","b") -> 'b a' 
print("My name is {} and I am {} years old".format("Ali", 25))
print("{0} + {1} = {2}".format(2, 3, 5))

docs.title: f-strings (Formatted String Literals)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose String ke andar directly variables/expressions daalne ka modern tareeqa Syntax f"text {variable}" Example f"My name is {name}" Output 'My name is Ali' When to use Hamesha — ye sabse fast aur readable tareeqa hai (Python 3.6+) Common Mistakes f prefix lagana bhool jaate hain, phir {name} literally print hota hai 
name = "Ali"
age = 25
print(f"My name is {name} and I am {age} years old")
print(f"Next year I will be {age + 1}")   # expressions bhi chal sakti hain
price = 49.999
print(f"Price: {price:.2f}")   # formatting: 'Price: 50.00'

💡 Tip: Real-world projects mein hamesha f-strings use karo — .format() aur % wala purana style avoid karo jab tak legacy code na ho.

docs.title: 2. Lists
docs.text: Lists ordered aur mutable (changeable) collections hain. [] se banti hain.

docs.title: append()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List ke akhir mein ek item add karta hai Syntax list.append(item) Example my_list.append(5) Output List mein 5 add ho jata hai akhir mein When to use Loop mein data collect karte waqt Common Mistakes append() return kuch nahi karta (None) — my_list = my_list.append(5) likhne se list None ban jayegi! 
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
fruits.append("mango")
print(fruits)  # ['apple', 'banana', 'mango']

docs.title: extend()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Ek list mein doosri list (ya iterable) ke saare items add karta hai Syntax list.extend(iterable) Example list1.extend(list2) Output list1 mein list2 ke saare elements add ho jaate hain When to use Do lists merge karne ke liye Common Mistakes append() use kar dete hain jisse poori list ek single item ban jati hai: [1,2].append([3,4]) -> [1,2,[3,4]] (galat agar merge chahiye) 
a = [1, 2]
b = [3, 4]
a.extend(b)
print(a)  # [1, 2, 3, 4]

# Difference from append:
x = [1, 2]
x.append([3, 4])
print(x)  # [1, 2, [3, 4]]  <- nested list

docs.title: insert()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Specific position par item add karta hai Syntax list.insert(index, item) Example list.insert(1, "new") Output Index 1 par "new" insert ho jata hai When to use Jab item ko specific jagah par daalna ho, akhir mein nahi Common Mistakes Index out of range hone par error nahi aata — Python automatically end ya start mein daal deta hai 
fruits = ["apple", "mango"]
fruits.insert(1, "banana")
print(fruits)  # ['apple', 'banana', 'mango']

docs.title: remove()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List se value ke basis par pehla matching item hata deta hai Syntax list.remove(value) Example fruits.remove("banana") Output "banana" list se hat jata hai When to use Jab value pata ho lekin index na pata ho Common Mistakes Agar value list mein nahi hai to ValueError aata hai 
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
fruits.remove("banana")
print(fruits)  # ['apple', 'mango']

docs.title: pop()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Index ke basis par item hata kar wo return bhi karta hai Syntax list.pop(index=-1) Example fruits.pop(0) Output Pehla item return hoga aur list se hat jayega When to use Jab item nikaalna ho aur uski value bhi chahiye ho (jaise stack/queue implementation) Common Mistakes Bina index diye pop() last item nikaalta hai, first nahi 
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
last = fruits.pop()
print(last)     # 'mango'
print(fruits)   # ['apple', 'banana']

docs.title: clear()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List ke saare elements hata deta hai (empty list bana deta hai) Syntax list.clear() Example fruits.clear() Output [] When to use List ko reset karne ke liye bina naya object banaye Common Mistakes fruits = [] alag hai (naya object banata hai), clear() same object ko empty karta hai — memory reference wale scenarios mein farq padta hai 
fruits = ["apple", "banana"]
fruits.clear()
print(fruits)  # []

docs.title: copy()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List ki shallow copy banata hai Syntax list.copy() Example new_list = old_list.copy() Output New independent list (top-level) When to use Jab original list ko safe rakhna ho, changes copy mein karni hon Common Mistakes new_list = old_list copy NAHI karta — dono same object ko point karte hain! Ye sabse common beginner mistake hai 
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a.copy()
b.append(4)
print(a)  # [1, 2, 3]      <- original safe
print(b)  # [1, 2, 3, 4]

# WRONG WAY:
c = a
c.append(99)
print(a)  # [1, 2, 3, 99]  <- 'a' bhi change ho gaya!

docs.title: reverse()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List ke elements ka order ulta kar deta hai (in-place) Syntax list.reverse() Example nums.reverse() Output List reverse order mein ho jati hai When to use Order palatne ke liye Common Mistakes Kuch return nahi karta — nums = nums.reverse() se None mil jayega 
nums = [1, 2, 3]
nums.reverse()
print(nums)  # [3, 2, 1]

docs.title: sort()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List ko in-place sort (order mein arrange) karta hai Syntax list.sort(key=None, reverse=False) Example nums.sort() Output Ascending order mein sorted list When to use Data ko order mein dikhane ke liye (numbers, names, etc.) Common Mistakes sort() original list ko change karta hai aur None return karta hai. Agar naya sorted result chahiye bina original change kiye, to sorted() function use karo 
nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
nums.sort()
print(nums)  # [1, 1, 3, 4, 5]

nums.sort(reverse=True)
print(nums)  # [5, 4, 3, 1, 1]

# Sorting with key
words = ["banana", "kiwi", "apple"]
words.sort(key=len)
print(words)  # ['kiwi', 'apple', 'banana']

docs.title: index() (for lists)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Value ki pehli occurrence ka index return karta hai Syntax list.index(value) Example fruits.index("banana") Output Index number When to use Jab position pata karni ho Common Mistakes Value na milne par ValueError aata hai 
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
print(fruits.index("banana"))  # 1

docs.title: count() (for lists)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List mein koi value kitni baar hai, wo ginta hai Syntax list.count(value) Example [1,2,2,3].count(2) Output 2 When to use Duplicate items count karne ke liye Common Mistakes Nested lists ke andar count nahi karta, sirf top-level 
nums = [1, 2, 2, 3, 2]
print(nums.count(2))  # 3

docs.title: Slicing
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose List (ya string) ka ek part/portion nikaalta hai Syntax list[start:stop:step] Example nums[1:4] Output Index 1 se 3 tak ke elements When to use Data ka subset nikaalne ke liye, list palatne ke liye ([::-1]) Common Mistakes stop index exclude hota hai — beginners sochte hain include hoga 
nums = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
print(nums[1:4])    # [20, 30, 40]
print(nums[:3])     # [10, 20, 30]
print(nums[2:])     # [30, 40, 50]
print(nums[::-1])   # [50, 40, 30, 20, 10]  (reverse trick)
print(nums[::2])    # [10, 30, 50]  (every 2nd element)

docs.title: List Comprehensions
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Ek line mein naya list banane ka short aur fast tareeqa Syntax [expression for item in iterable if condition] Example [x*2 for x in range(5)] Output [0, 2, 4, 6, 8] When to use Jab loop se list banani ho — cleaner aur faster hai normal for-loop se Common Mistakes Zyada complex logic ko comprehension mein daal dena — readability kharab ho jati hai. Simple cases ke liye hi use karo 
squares = [x**2 for x in range(5)]
print(squares)  # [0, 1, 4, 9, 16]

# With condition
evens = [x for x in range(10) if x % 2 == 0]
print(evens)  # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]

# Real-world example: cleaning data
names = ["  ali", "SARA  ", "zain"]
cleaned = [n.strip().title() for n in names]
print(cleaned)  # ['Ali', 'Sara', 'Zain']

docs.title: 3. Dictionaries
docs.text: Dictionaries key: value pairs store karti hain. {} se banti hain. Fast lookup ke liye best hain.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Key ki value nikaalta hai, agar key na ho to error ki jagah default value deta hai Syntax dict.get(key, default=None) Example person.get("age", 0) Output Agar "age" key hai to uski value, warna 0 When to use Hamesha jab pakka na ho ke key exist karti hai — crash se bachata hai Common Mistakes dict["key"] use karna jab key exist na ho -> KeyError crash 
person = {"name": "Ali", "age": 25}
print(person.get("age"))          # 25
print(person.get("city"))         # None
print(person.get("city", "N/A"))  # 'N/A'

docs.title: keys()
values()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Dictionary ki saari values return karta hai Syntax dict.values() Example person.values() Output dict_values(['Ali', 25]) When to use Sirf values chahiye hon, keys nahi Common Mistakes Purane code mein order guaranteed nahi tha (Python 3.7+ mein insertion order fix hai) 
print(list(person.values()))  # ['Ali', 25]

docs.title: items()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Key-value pairs ek saath (tuples ki form mein) return karta hai Syntax dict.items() Example for k, v in person.items(): Output Har pair (key, value) When to use Loop mein key aur value dono chahiye hon Common Mistakes for k, v in person: likhna (bina .items()) — error aata hai 
for key, value in person.items():
    print(f"{key}: {value}")
# name: Ali
# age: 25

4. Sets

remove()

5. Tuples
docs.text: Tuples immutable ordered collections hain. Ek baar ban gayi to change nahi ho sakti.

docs.title: count() (for tuple)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Tuple mein value kitni baar aati hai Syntax tuple.count(value) Example (1,2,2,3).count(2) Output 2 When to use Fixed data mein frequency check karne ke liye Common Mistakes List ke count() jaisa hi lagta hai — bas tuple modify nahi ho sakti 
t = (1, 2, 2, 3, 2)
print(t.count(2))  # 3

docs.title: index() (for tuple)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Value ki pehli position return karta hai Syntax tuple.index(value) Example (10,20,30).index(20) Output 1 When to use Position pata karni ho Common Mistakes Value na milne par ValueError 
t = (10, 20, 30)
print(t.index(20))  # 1

💡 Tuple vs List: Tuple immutable hai (fast/safe, jab data change nahi hona chahiye — jaise coordinates (x, y)), List mutable hai (jab data change hoga).

docs.title: 6. Built-in Functions
docs.text: Ye woh functions hain jo Python mein directly available hain, bina import kiye.

docs.title: len()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kisi bhi collection (string, list, dict, etc.) ki length (size) batata hai Syntax len(object) Example len([1,2,3]) Output 3 When to use Har jagah — validation, loops, conditions Common Mistakes None par call karne se error aata hai 
print(len("hello"))       # 5
print(len([1, 2, 3]))     # 3
print(len({"a": 1, "b": 2}))  # 2

docs.title: type()
isinstance()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai object kisi particular type ka hai ya nahi Syntax isinstance(object, type) Example isinstance(5, int) Output True When to use Type checking ke liye — type() == se better hai Common Mistakes Tuple of types bhi de sakte ho: isinstance(x, (int, float)) — beginners iska pata nahi hota 
print(isinstance(5, int))          # True
print(isinstance(5, (int, float))) # True
print(isinstance("hi", str))       # True

docs.title: print()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Output screen par dikhata hai Syntax print(*values, sep=' ', end='\n') Example print("Hello", "World", sep="-") Output Hello-World When to use Debugging, output display karne ke liye Common Mistakes sep aur end parameters ke baare mein pata nahi hota beginners ko 
print("Hello", "World")             # Hello World
print("Hello", "World", sep="-")    # Hello-World
print("Loading", end="...")          # Loading... (no newline)

docs.title: input()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose User se keyboard input leta hai Syntax input(prompt) Example name = input("Enter name: ") Output Jo user type kare wo string ban jata hai When to use Console-based programs mein user se data lene ke liye Common Mistakes input() hamesha string return karta hai — numbers ke liye int(input()) karna padta hai 
age = input("Enter your age: ")
print(type(age))         # <class 'str'> (even if user typed 25)
age = int(input("Enter your age: "))
print(type(age))         # <class 'int'>

docs.title: range()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Numbers ki ek sequence generate karta hai (loops ke liye) Syntax range(start, stop, step) Example range(0, 10, 2) Output 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 When to use For loops mein kitni baar repeat karna hai, ye decide karne ke liye Common Mistakes stop value exclude hoti hai — range(5) 0 se 4 tak jayega, 5 tak nahi 
for i in range(5):
    print(i)  # 0 1 2 3 4

for i in range(2, 10, 2):
    print(i)  # 2 4 6 8

docs.title: enumerate()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Loop mein item ke saath uska index bhi deta hai Syntax enumerate(iterable, start=0) Example for i, val in enumerate(["a","b"]): Output 0 a 1 b When to use Jab loop mein index bhi chahiye ho — manual counter (i = 0; i += 1) ki zaroorat khatam kar deta hai Common Mistakes for i in enumerate(list): likhna aur phir i ko value samajhna — actually i tuple hota hai (index, value) 
fruits = ["apple", "banana", "mango"]
for index, fruit in enumerate(fruits):
    print(index, fruit)
# 0 apple
# 1 banana
# 2 mango

for index, fruit in enumerate(fruits, start=1):
    print(index, fruit)  # 1 apple, 2 banana, 3 mango

docs.title: zip()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Do (ya zyada) lists ko parallel combine karta hai Syntax zip(iterable1, iterable2, ...) Example zip([1,2],["a","b"]) Output (1,'a'), (2,'b') When to use Do related lists ko ek saath loop karne ke liye Common Mistakes Agar lists ki length different ho to shortest list ke hisaab se stop ho jata hai — extra items silently drop ho jaate hain 
names = ["Ali", "Sara"]
ages = [25, 22]
for name, age in zip(names, ages):
    print(f"{name} is {age} years old")
# Ali is 25 years old
# Sara is 22 years old

# converting to dict
print(dict(zip(names, ages)))  # {'Ali': 25, 'Sara': 22}

docs.title: map()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Har item par ek function apply karta hai aur naya iterable return karta hai Syntax map(function, iterable) Example map(str.upper, ["a","b"]) Output ['A', 'B'] (list() se convert karne ke baad) When to use Poori list par ek transformation apply karni ho, bina explicit loop likhe Common Mistakes map() khud print nahi hota — list() se convert karna padta hai kyunki ye ek "lazy" map object return karta hai 
nums = [1, 2, 3]
squared = list(map(lambda x: x**2, nums))
print(squared)  # [1, 4, 9]

docs.title: filter()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Condition ke basis par items ko filter karta hai Syntax filter(function, iterable) Example filter(lambda x: x>2, [1,2,3,4]) Output [3, 4] (list() se convert karne ke baad) When to use List se sirf wo items chahiye jo condition satisfy karte hain Common Mistakes map() ki tarah ye bhi lazy hai — list() mein wrap karna zaroori hai 
nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
evens = list(filter(lambda x: x % 2 == 0, nums))
print(evens)  # [2, 4, 6]

docs.title: sorted()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Naya sorted list return karta hai, original change nahi hota Syntax sorted(iterable, key=None, reverse=False) Example sorted([3,1,2]) Output [1, 2, 3] When to use Jab original data safe rakhna ho, sirf sorted copy chahiye ho Common Mistakes list.sort() se confuse hote hain — sort() list ka method hai (in-place), sorted() ek function hai (naya object return karta hai, kisi bhi iterable par kaam karta hai) 
nums = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
print(sorted(nums))            # [1, 1, 3, 4, 5]
print(nums)                    # [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]  (unchanged!)
print(sorted(nums, reverse=True))  # [5, 4, 3, 1, 1]

people = [{"name": "Ali", "age": 25}, {"name": "Sara", "age": 22}]
print(sorted(people, key=lambda p: p["age"]))

docs.title: sum()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Numbers ki list ka total deta hai Syntax sum(iterable, start=0) Example sum([1,2,3]) Output 6 When to use Total calculate karne ke liye (bill total, scores, etc.) Common Mistakes Strings ke sath use karne ki koshish karna -> error (sum(["a","b"]) kaam nahi karega) 
print(sum([1, 2, 3, 4]))  # 10
print(sum([1, 2, 3], 10))  # 16 (start=10)

docs.title: min()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Sabse choti value return karta hai Syntax min(iterable) Example min([3,1,2]) Output 1 When to use Smallest value dhoondne ke liye Common Mistakes Empty list par call karne se error aata hai 
print(min([3, 1, 4, 1, 5]))  # 1
print(min("banana"))          # 'a'

docs.title: max()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Sabse badi value return karta hai Syntax max(iterable) Example max([3,1,2]) Output 3 When to use Largest value dhoondne ke liye Common Mistakes Different types mix karne se error aata hai (max([1, "a"]) fail hoga) 
print(max([3, 1, 4, 1, 5]))  # 5

docs.title: any()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai kya iterable mein koi bhi ek value True hai Syntax any(iterable) Example any([False, False, True]) Output True When to use Jab check karna ho ke condition kam se kam ek jagah satisfy hoti hai Common Mistakes Empty iterable par False return karta hai — beginners True expect karte hain 
nums = [0, 0, 3, 0]
print(any(nums))  # True (kyunki 3 non-zero hai)
print(any([x > 10 for x in [1, 2, 3]]))  # False

docs.title: all()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai kya iterable ke saare values True hain Syntax all(iterable) Example all([True, True, True]) Output True When to use Jab check karna ho ke saari conditions satisfy hoti hain Common Mistakes Empty iterable par True return karta hai (opposite of any()) — confusing lag sakta hai 
print(all([True, True, False]))  # False
print(all([x > 0 for x in [1, 2, 3]]))  # True

docs.title: abs()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kisi number ki absolute (positive) value deta hai Syntax abs(number) Example abs(-5) Output 5 When to use Negative differences ko positive banane ke liye Common Mistakes Strings par use karne ki koshish karna -> error 
print(abs(-5))    # 5
print(abs(5))     # 5
print(abs(-3.14)) # 3.14

docs.title: round()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Number ko given decimal places tak round karta hai Syntax round(number, digits=0) Example round(3.14159, 2) Output 3.14 When to use Money, percentages, ya kisi bhi precision-controlled output ke liye Common Mistakes Python "banker's rounding" use karta hai: round(2.5) -> 2 (not 3!) — ye surprise deta hai beginners ko 
print(round(3.14159, 2))  # 3.14
print(round(2.5))          # 2  (banker's rounding!)
print(round(3.5))          # 4

docs.title: open()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose File ko open karta hai (read/write ke liye) Syntax open(filename, mode) Example open("data.txt", "r") Output File object return hota hai When to use File se data read/write karne ke liye Common Mistakes File ko close karna bhool jaana — with open() use karo taake automatically close ho jaye 
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
print(content)

docs.title: id()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Object ka unique memory address (identity) deta hai Syntax id(object) Example id(x) Output Ek unique integer number When to use Debugging ke liye, ya check karna ke do variables same object hain ya alag Common Mistakes Real-world projects mein rarely use hota hai — mostly learning/debugging ke liye 
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
print(id(a) == id(b))  # True (same object)
c = a.copy()
print(id(a) == id(c))  # False (different object)

docs.title: dir()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Object ke saare available attributes/methods list karta hai Syntax dir(object) Example dir([]) Output List methods jaise ['append', 'clear', ...] When to use Explore karne ke liye ke koi object kya kya kar sakta hai Common Mistakes Bohot saare "dunder" methods (__init__ etc.) bhi show karta hai jo confusing lag sakte hain 
print(dir([]))  # shows all list methods

docs.title: help()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kisi function/module ki documentation dikhata hai Syntax help(object) Example help(str.upper) Output Documentation text When to use Jab kisi function ke baare mein detail chahiye ho, bina internet ke Common Mistakes Interactive terminal mein best kaam karta hai; scripts mein use karna common nahi hai 
help(str.upper)

docs.title: vars()
repr()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Object ki developer-friendly string representation deta hai Syntax repr(object) Example repr("hello") Output "'hello'" (quotes ke saath) When to use Debugging ke liye, jab exact data type/format dekhna ho Common Mistakes str() se confuse hote hain — str() user-friendly hota hai, repr() debug-friendly 
print(str("hello"))   # hello
print(repr("hello"))  # 'hello'

docs.title: str(), int(), float(), bool() (Type Conversion)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Data ko doosre type mein convert karte hain Syntax str(x), int(x), float(x), bool(x) Example int("25") Output 25 (as integer) When to use User input, file data, ya API response ko sahi type mein convert karne ke liye Common Mistakes int("25.5") fail hoga — pehle float() phir int() karna padega. bool("False") -> True hai! (kyunki non-empty string hamesha truthy hoti hai) 
print(int("25"))       # 25
print(str(25))          # '25'
print(float("3.14"))    # 3.14
print(bool(""))          # False
print(bool("False"))     # True  <- tricky!
print(bool(0))           # False
print(bool(1))           # True

docs.title: list(), tuple(), set(), dict() (Collection Conversion)
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kisi iterable ko given collection type mein convert karte hain Syntax list(x), tuple(x), set(x), dict(x) Example list("abc") Output ['a', 'b', 'c'] When to use Data structure conversion ke liye (jaise duplicates hatane ke liye set()) Common Mistakes dict() ko random list se banane ki koshish karna — dict banane ke liye pairs (tuples) chahiye 
print(list("abc"))              # ['a', 'b', 'c']
print(tuple([1, 2, 3]))          # (1, 2, 3)
print(set([1, 1, 2, 2, 3]))      # {1, 2, 3}  <- duplicates removed
print(dict([("a", 1), ("b", 2)]))  # {'a': 1, 'b': 2}

docs.title: for
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kisi iterable (list, string, range, etc.) ke har item par repeat karta hai Syntax for item in iterable: Example for i in range(3): print(i) Output 0 1 2 When to use Jab pata ho kitni baar ya kis cheez par loop chalana hai Common Mistakes Colon : bhoolna, ya indentation galat karna 
for fruit in ["apple", "banana"]:
    print(fruit)

docs.title: while
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Jab tak condition True hai, tab tak repeat karta hai Syntax while condition: Example while x < 5: Output Condition false hone tak chalta rehta hai When to use Jab pata na ho kitni baar loop chalega, sirf condition pata ho Common Mistakes Infinite loop — counter update karna bhool jaana 
x = 0
while x < 5:
    print(x)
    x += 1  # yeh na likhein to infinite loop ban jayega

docs.title: break
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Loop ko turant rok deta hai Syntax break Example if x == 5: break Output Loop wahin exit ho jata hai When to use Jab koi condition mile aur loop continue karne ki zaroorat na ho Common Mistakes Nested loops mein break sirf innermost loop ko rokta hai, outer loop chalta rehta hai 
for i in range(10):
    if i == 5:
        break
    print(i)  # 0 1 2 3 4

docs.title: continue
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Current iteration skip karke agli iteration par chala jata hai Syntax continue Example if x % 2 == 0: continue Output Us particular value ko skip karke aage badh jata hai When to use Kisi specific case ko skip karna ho lekin loop continue rakhna ho Common Mistakes break se confuse hote hain — continue loop rokta nahi, sirf ek iteration skip karta hai 
for i in range(5):
    if i == 2:
        continue
    print(i)  # 0 1 3 4  (2 skip ho gaya)

docs.title: pass
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Kuch bhi nahi karta — sirf placeholder hota hai Syntax pass Example if x: pass Output Koi output nahi, code sirf syntactically valid rehta hai When to use Jab function/class/loop ka structure likhna ho lekin logic baad mein likhna ho Common Mistakes pass aur continue ko confuse karna — pass kuch nahi karta, bas syntax error se bachata hai 
def my_function():
    pass  # TODO: implement later

for i in range(5):
    if i == 2:
        pass  # nothing happens, loop continues normally
    print(i)

docs.title: if / elif / else
def
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Naya function define karta hai Syntax def function_name(parameters): Example def greet(name): print(f"Hello {name}") Output Function call hone par output When to use Reusable code blocks banane ke liye Common Mistakes Colon bhoolna, indentation galat karna 
def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")

greet("Ali")  # Hello, Ali!

docs.title: return
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Function se value wapas bhejta hai Syntax return value Example return x + y Output Function call karne wali jagah par value milti hai When to use Jab function ka result use karna ho Common Mistakes return ke baad ka code kabhi nahi chalta (function turant exit ho jata hai). print() aur return confuse karna — print() sirf dikhata hai, return value deta hai use karne ke liye 
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(2, 3)
print(result)  # 5

docs.title: *args
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Function ko koi bhi number of positional arguments accept karne deta hai Syntax def func(*args): Example def total(*args): return sum(args) Output args ek tuple ban jata hai saare arguments ka When to use Jab pata na ho kitne arguments aayenge Common Mistakes args ko list samajh lena — actually ye tuple hai 
def total(*args):
    return sum(args)

print(total(1, 2, 3))       # 6
print(total(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) # 15

docs.title: **kwargs
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Function ko koi bhi number of keyword arguments accept karne deta hai Syntax def func(**kwargs): Example def info(**kwargs): print(kwargs) Output kwargs ek dictionary ban jata hai When to use Jab named arguments ki flexible number chahiye ho (jaise config options) Common Mistakes Order guaranteed nahi tha purane Python mein, lekin 3.7+ mein insertion order preserve hoti hai 
def show_info(**kwargs):
    for key, value in kwargs.items():
        print(f"{key}: {value}")

show_info(name="Ali", age=25, city="Lahore")
# name: Ali
# age: 25
# city: Lahore

docs.title: lambda
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Anonymous (bina naam ki) chhoti function banata hai, ek line mein Syntax lambda arguments: expression Example lambda x: x * 2 Output Function object jo call hone par result deta hai When to use Chhote, one-time-use functions ke liye (jaise sort(), map(), filter() ke saath) Common Mistakes Complex logic lambda mein daalne ki koshish karna — lambda sirf single expression support karta hai, statements (if/for blocks) nahi 
square = lambda x: x ** 2
print(square(5))  # 25

# Common use with sort
people = [{"name": "Ali", "age": 25}, {"name": "Sara", "age": 22}]
people.sort(key=lambda p: p["age"])
print(people)

docs.title: class
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Naya blueprint (class) define karta hai objects banane ke liye Syntax class ClassName: Example class Car: Output Class definition, objects banane ke liye ready When to use Jab related data aur functions ko ek unit mein rakhna ho (OOP) Common Mistakes Class name convention PascalCase hota hai (jaise MyClass), lowercase use karna style guideline violate karta hai 
class Car:
    def __init__(self, brand):
        self.brand = brand

    def show(self):
        print(f"This car is a {self.brand}")

my_car = Car("Toyota")
my_car.show()  # This car is a Toyota

docs.title: __init__
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Class ka constructor — object banate waqt automatically call hota hai Syntax def __init__(self, params): Example def __init__(self, name): self.name = name Output Object ban jata hai apni initial values ke saath When to use Object create hote hi jo initial setup chahiye (jaise attributes set karna) Common Mistakes self parameter likhna bhool jaana 
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name, age):
        self.name = name
        self.age = age

p = Person("Ali", 25)
print(p.name)  # Ali

docs.title: self
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Current object (instance) ko refer karta hai class ke andar Syntax Har method ka pehla parameter Example def greet(self): print(self.name) Output Object ke apne attributes access ho jaate hain When to use Har instance method mein zaroori hai Common Mistakes self likhna bhool jaana class methods mein — error aayega 
class Dog:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

    def bark(self):
        print(f"{self.name} says Woof!")

d = Dog("Rex")
d.bark()  # Rex says Woof!

docs.title: Inheritance
super()
try / except / finally
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Errors ko handle karta hai bina program crash kiye Syntax try: ... except Error: ... finally: ... Example try: 1/0 except ZeroDivisionError: print("Error") Output Error catch ho jata hai, program crash nahi hota When to use Jahan error aane ka chance ho (file operations, API calls, user input, division) Common Mistakes Bina specific exception type diye bare except: likhna — ye sab errors silently hide kar deta hai jo debugging mushkil bana deta hai 
try:
    result = 10 / 0
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Cannot divide by zero!")
finally:
    print("This always runs")

# Better practice: specific exceptions
try:
    num = int(input("Enter a number: "))
except ValueError:
    print("That's not a valid number!")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Something went wrong: {e}")
finally:
    print("Done trying")

docs.title: raise
with open()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose File ko safely open karta hai aur kaam khatam hone par automatically close kar deta hai Syntax with open(filename, mode) as f: Example with open("data.txt", "r") as f: Output File object f milta hai use karne ke liye When to use Hamesha file open karte waqt — open() akela use karke close() bhoolne se bacha jata hai Common Mistakes with use na karke sirf f = open(...) likhna aur f.close() bhool jaana — file locked reh sakti hai 
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
print(content)
# file yahan automatically close ho chuki hoti hai

docs.title: read()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Poori file ka content ek single string mein padhta hai Syntax file.read(size=-1) Example f.read() Output Poora file content as string When to use Choti files ke liye jab poora content ek sath chahiye ho Common Mistakes Badi files par read() use karna — memory bhar sakti hai. Bari files ke liye line-by-line read karo 
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    text = f.read()
print(text)

docs.title: readline()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose File se sirf ek line padhta hai Syntax file.readline() Example f.readline() Output Ek line as string (with \n) When to use Jab line-by-line control chahiye ho Common Mistakes Bar bar call karna zaroori hai agli lines ke liye — loop mein use karna common hai 
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    first_line = f.readline()
    print(first_line)

docs.title: readlines()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Poori file ko list of lines mein padhta hai Syntax file.readlines() Example f.readlines() Output ['line1\n', 'line2\n', ...] When to use Jab har line ko separately process karna ho Common Mistakes Har line ke saath \n bhi aata hai — beginners bhool jaate hain .strip() karna 
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    lines = f.readlines()
for line in lines:
    print(line.strip())

docs.title: write()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose File mein ek string likhta hai Syntax file.write(text) Example f.write("Hello\n") Output File mein text add ho jata hai When to use File mein data save karne ke liye Common Mistakes Mode "w" use karna file ko overwrite kar deta hai — agar add karna ho to "a" (append) mode use karo 
with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Hello World\n")

# Appending instead of overwriting
with open("output.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("Another line\n")

docs.title: writelines()
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Multiple lines (list of strings) file mein ek sath likhta hai Syntax file.writelines(list_of_strings) Example f.writelines(["a ", "b "]) Output File mein saari lines add ho jaati hain When to use Jab list of strings ko efficiently file mein daalna ho Common Mistakes Ye automatically add nahi karta — khud add karna padta hai har string ke akhir mein 
lines = ["Line 1
", "Line 2
", "Line 3
"]
with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    f.writelines(lines)

File Modes Quick Reference:

Mode Matlab "r" Read (default) "w" Write (overwrite karta hai) "a" Append (end mein add karta hai) "r+" Read + Write "rb" / "wb" Binary mode (images, PDFs ke liye)

docs.title: import
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Doosri file/library ka code use karne ke liye Syntax import module_name Example import math Output Module ke functions available ho jaate hain When to use Jab external libraries (jaise os, math, requests) use karni hon Common Mistakes Module install na hone par ModuleNotFoundError — pip install module_name karna padta hai pehle 
import math
print(math.sqrt(16))  # 4.0

docs.title: from ... import ...
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Poore module ki bajaye sirf specific cheez import karta hai Syntax from module import name Example from math import sqrt Output Ab sqrt() direct use kar sakte ho bina math. likhe When to use Jab poori library nahi, sirf ek function/class chahiye Common Mistakes Bohot saare imports ek saath karna aur naming conflicts create karna 
from math import sqrt, pi
print(sqrt(16))  # 4.0
print(pi)          # 3.14159...

docs.title: as
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Import kiye gaye module/function ko ek alias (nickname) deta hai Syntax import module as alias Example import pandas as pd Output Ab pd se poora pandas module access hota hai When to use Lambe naam wale modules ke liye shorthand banane ke liye (common convention) Common Mistakes Bohot ajeeb/confusing alias choose karna jo koi aur samajh na paye 
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

arr = np.array([1, 2, 3])

docs.title: async / await
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Asynchronous code likhne ke liye — ek kaam ka wait karte hue doosra kaam bhi ho sakta hai Syntax async def func(): ... await something Example async def get_data(): result = await fetch() Output Function bina block kiye chalta hai When to use APIs, database calls, ya kisi bhi "waiting" operation mein — jaise FastAPI endpoints, web scraping, multiple API calls parallel mein Common Mistakes async def function ko bina await ya event loop ke normal function ki tarah call karna — result milta hai ek "coroutine object", actual value nahi 
import asyncio

async def fetch_data():
    await asyncio.sleep(2)  # simulate waiting (jaise API call)
    return "Data received"

async def main():
    result = await fetch_data()
    print(result)

asyncio.run(main())

💡 Real-world use: FastAPI mein async def endpoints likhe jaate hain taake server ek request ka wait kartay hue doosri requests bhi handle kar sake.

from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/data")
async def get_data():
    # yahan koi async database call ya API call ho sakti hai
    return {"message": "Hello"}

docs.title: in
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai koi value kisi collection mein maujood hai ya nahi Syntax value in collection Example "a" in [1, "a", 2] Output True When to use Membership check ke liye — lists, strings, dicts (keys check karta hai), sets Common Mistakes Dictionary mein in sirf keys check karta hai, values nahi 
print(3 in [1, 2, 3])         # True
print("a" in "banana")         # True
d = {"name": "Ali"}
print("name" in d)              # True (checks keys)
print("Ali" in d)                # False (Ali is a value, not key)

docs.title: not in
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai value collection mein maujood nahi hai Syntax value not in collection Example 5 not in [1,2,3] Output True When to use Jab confirm karna ho ke koi cheez missing hai Common Mistakes not (x in y) aur x not in y same result dete hain, lekin not in zyada readable hai 
print(5 not in [1, 2, 3])  # True

docs.title: is
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai do variables same object hain (memory mein) Syntax a is b Example x is None Output True/False When to use None check karne ke liye hamesha is use karo, == nahi Common Mistakes is ko == ki jagah values compare karne ke liye use karna — is identity check karta hai, value equality nahi 
x = None
print(x is None)   # True (correct way)

a = [1, 2, 3]
b = [1, 2, 3]
print(a == b)  # True  (same values)
print(a is b)  # False (different objects in memory)

docs.title: is not
docs.text:
Field Details Purpose Check karta hai do variables alag object hain Syntax a is not b Example x is not None Output True/False When to use None check ke opposite case ke liye Common Mistakes != se confuse hote hain — is not identity, != value inequality check karta hai 
x = 5
if x is not None:
    print("x has a value")

docs.title: 16. Common Real-World Methods
docs.text:
Ye methods aksar real projects, APIs aur libraries mein baar baar dikhte hain.

Method Kahan milta hai Kya karta hai .strip() Text cleaning Extra spaces hatata hai .json() requests library (API responses) API response ko Python dict mein convert karta hai .text requests library Response ka raw text (string) deta hai .items() Dictionaries Key-value pairs loop karne ke liye .get() Dictionaries, APIs, Django ORM Safe value fetch karta hai .copy() Lists, Dicts Shallow copy banata hai .update() Dictionaries Values update/add karta hai .append() Lists Naya item add karta hai .sort() Lists List ko order mein arrange karta hai .reverse() Lists Order ulta karta hai

docs.title: .json() aur .text (requests library se)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/users")

print(response.text)   # raw string response
print(response.json()) # parsed as Python dict/list
Field Details Purpose .json() API response ko Python object (dict/list) mein convert karta hai, .text raw string deta hai When to use .json() jab response JSON format mein ho (aksar hota hai), .text jab HTML/plain text chahiye Common Mistakes .json() call karna jab response actually JSON na ho — JSONDecodeError aayega

docs.title: 17. Python You'll See Every Day in Real Projects
17.1 FastAPI
docs.text:
FastAPI mein aksar ye patterns dikhte hain:

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

@app.get("/")
def home():
    return {"message": "Welcome"}

@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
async def get_user(user_id: int):
    if user_id <= 0:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Ali"}

@app.post("/users")
async def create_user(user: User):
    return {"message": f"User {user.name} created"}
  • @app.get(), @app.post() — decorators jo route define karte hain
  • BaseModel — Pydantic se data validation ke liye
  • async def — non-blocking endpoints ke liye
  • HTTPException — proper error response bhejne ke liye

docs.title: 17.2 Django
docs.text:
from django.db import models
from django.shortcuts import render, get_object_or_404

class Product(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    price = models.FloatField()

def product_detail(request, pk):
    product = get_object_or_404(Product, pk=pk)
    return render(request, "product.html", {"product": product})
  • models.Model — database table define karne ke liye
  • get_object_or_404() — object na milne par automatically 404 error deta hai
  • render() — HTML template ko response ke saath bhejta hai

docs.title: 17.3 Flask
docs.text:
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/hello", methods=["GET"])
def hello():
    return jsonify({"message": "Hello World"})

@app.route("/data", methods=["POST"])
def receive_data():
    data = request.json
    return jsonify({"received": data})

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)
  • jsonify() — Python dict ko JSON response mein convert karta hai
  • request.json — incoming request ka JSON body
  • app.run(debug=True) — development server chalata hai (auto-reload ke saath)

docs.title: 17.4 AI Projects
docs.text:
import numpy as np

data = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
print(data.mean())    # average
print(data.std())     # standard deviation

# Common pattern: preprocessing
normalized = (data - data.min()) / (data.max() - data.min())
print(normalized)
  • numpy — numerical operations ke liye
  • .mean(), .std() — statistics calculate karne ke liye
  • Data normalization/scaling AI projects mein bohot common hai

docs.title: 17.5 LangChain
docs.text:
from langchain.prompts import PromptTemplate
from langchain.chains import LLMChain
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4", temperature=0)

prompt = PromptTemplate(
    input_variables=["topic"],
    template="Write a short summary about {topic}"
)

chain = LLMChain(llm=llm, prompt=prompt)
result = chain.run(topic="Python programming")
print(result)
  • PromptTemplate — dynamic prompts banane ke liye
  • LLMChain — prompt + model ko combine karta hai ek "chain" mein
  • .run() — chain execute karta hai aur result deta hai

docs.title: 17.6 LangGraph
docs.text:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END

def node_a(state):
    state["count"] += 1
    return state

def should_continue(state):
    return "continue" if state["count"] < 3 else "end"

graph = StateGraph(dict)
graph.add_node("a", node_a)
graph.set_entry_point("a")
graph.add_conditional_edges("a", should_continue, {"continue": "a", "end": END})

app = graph.compile()
result = app.invoke({"count": 0})
print(result)  # {'count': 3}
  • StateGraph — AI agent ke steps (nodes) ka flow define karta hai
  • add_conditional_edges() — condition ke basis par next step decide karta hai
  • Ye agent workflows banane ke liye use hota hai (loops, decisions)

docs.title: 17.7 OpenAI Agents SDK
docs.text:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is Python?"}
    ]
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
  • client.chat.completions.create() — model ko call karne ka main function
  • messages — conversation history ka list
  • response.choices[0].message.content — actual reply text yahan milta hai

docs.title: 17.8 File Handling in Projects
docs.text:
import os

# Check if file exists before reading
if os.path.exists("config.json"):
    with open("config.json", "r") as f:
        data = f.read()

# Working with paths
folder = "uploads"
filename = "report.pdf"
full_path = os.path.join(folder, filename)
print(full_path)  # uploads/report.pdf

docs.title: 17.9 APIs (requests library)
docs.text:
import requests

response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/data", params={"page": 1})

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print(data)
else:
    print(f"Error: {response.status_code}")

# POST request
payload = {"name": "Ali", "email": "ali@example.com"}
response = requests.post("https://api.example.com/users", json=payload)
  • response.status_code — HTTP status check karne ke liye (200 = success)
  • params — URL query parameters bhejne ke liye
  • json=payload — request body ko JSON format mein bhejta hai automatically

docs.title: 17.10 JSON
docs.text:
import json

# Python dict -> JSON string
data = {"name": "Ali", "age": 25}
json_string = json.dumps(data)
print(json_string)  # '{"name": "Ali", "age": 25}'

# JSON string -> Python dict
parsed = json.loads(json_string)
print(parsed["name"])  # Ali

# Read/write JSON files
with open("data.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(data, f)

with open("data.json", "r") as f:
    loaded = json.load(f)
Function Kya karta hai json.dumps() Python object -> JSON string json.loads() JSON string -> Python object json.dump() Python object -> JSON file json.load() JSON file -> Python object

💡 Memory trick: "s" wale functions (dumps, loads) strings ke saath kaam karte hain. Bina "s" wale (dump, load) files ke saath.

docs.title: 17.11 Databases
docs.text:
import sqlite3

# Connect to database
conn = sqlite3.connect("app.db")
cursor = conn.cursor()

# Create table
cursor.execute("""
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        name TEXT
    )
""")

# Insert data
cursor.execute("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (?)", ("Ali",))
conn.commit()

# Read data
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users")
rows = cursor.fetchall()
print(rows)

conn.close()
  • cursor.execute() — SQL query run karta hai
  • conn.commit() — changes ko permanently save karta hai (isko bhoolna common mistake hai!)
  • cursor.fetchall() — saare results ek list mein deta hai
  • ? placeholders use karo direct string formatting ki bajaye — ye SQL injection se bachata hai
# ORM example (SQLAlchemy style, jaise Django/FastAPI mein use hota hai)
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

def get_user(db: Session, user_id: int):
    return db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()

docs.title: 18. One-Page Quick Revision Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
STRINGS          strip() lstrip() rstrip() split() join() replace()
                 find() index() startswith() endswith() lower() upper()
                 title() capitalize() count() f"{var}"

LISTS            append() extend() insert() remove() pop() clear()
                 copy() reverse() sort() index() count() list[a:b]
                 [x for x in items]  <- comprehension

DICTS            get() keys() values() items() update() pop()
                 popitem() setdefault() clear() copy()

SETS             add() remove() discard() union() intersection()
                 difference()  |  &  -

TUPLES           count() index()   <- immutable, cannot change

BUILT-INS        len() type() isinstance() print() input() range()
                 enumerate() zip() map() filter() sorted() sum()
                 min() max() any() all() abs() round() open()

LOOPS/COND       for while break continue pass if elif else

FUNCTIONS        def return *args **kwargs lambda

CLASSES          class __init__ self super() inheritance

ERRORS           try except finally raise

FILES            with open() read() readline() readlines()
                 write() writelines()

MODULES          import  from x import y  import x as y

ASYNC            async def ... await ...

OPERATORS        in  not in  is  is not

JSON             json.dumps() json.loads() json.dump() json.load()

APIs             requests.get() requests.post() .json() .status_code

Golden Rules to Remember: 1. sort() changes original list, sorted() makes a new one 2. copy() list/dict, mat direct = use karo agar independent copy chahiye 3. dict.get() safe hai, dict["key"] risky hai 4. is identity check, == value check 5. async def ke andar await zaroori hai actual result ke liye 6. File open karne ke liye hamesha with open() use karo

docs.title: 21. Interview Tips for Each Important Function
docs.text: Function/Concept Interview Tip sort() vs sorted() Hamesha bolo: "sort() in-place hai aur None return karta hai, sorted() naya list return karta hai" is vs == Bolo: "is identity check karta hai (memory address), == value check karta hai" Mutable vs Immutable List/Dict/Set = mutable, String/Tuple/Int = immutable — example ke saath explain karo *args vs **kwargs args = positional (tuple), kwargs = keyword (dict) — dono ka use case bolna zaroori hai append() vs extend() append ek item add karta hai (even if list), extend elements merge karta hai deep copy vs shallow copy shallow copy sirf top-level copy karta hai, nested objects same reference rehte hain — copy.deepcopy() bolna important hai Exception Handling Specific exceptions catch karna best practice hai, generic except: avoid karo — bolo "fail fast, fail clear" lambda Bolo: "single expression ke liye hai, complex logic ke liye normal function better hai" List Comprehension Bolo: "readability aur performance dono behtar hoti hai simple loops ke comparison mein" GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) Agar multi-threading pucha jaye, bolo "Python GIL ki wajah se true parallel threading CPU-bound tasks mein nahi hoti, isliye multiprocessing use karte hain" async/await Bolo: "I/O-bound tasks (API calls, DB queries) ke liye best hai, CPU-bound ke liye nahi" self keyword Bolo: "current instance ko refer karta hai, Python explicitly pass karta hai jabke doosri languages mein implicit hota hai" __init__ vs __new__ Advanced question — bolo "__new__ object create karta hai, __init__ usko initialize karta hai" Generators (yield) Bolo: "memory-efficient hain kyunki poori list memory mein nahi rakhte, ek time par ek value generate karte hain"

docs.title: 22. Memory Tricks (Yaad Rakhne Ke Tarike)
docs.text: Confusing Pair Trick append() vs extend() Append = Add one thing. Extend = Expand with many things remove() vs pop() remove() = value se dhoondo (remove by value). pop() = position se nikalo (pop by position) find() vs index() find() friendly hai (error nahi deta, -1 deta hai). index() impatient hai (error de deta hai) sort() vs sorted() sort() same list ko badalta hai. sorted() separate naya banata hai is vs == is = "identical object hai kya?" == = "value same hai kya?" get() vs [] get() = "gentle" (safe, default deta hai). [] = "brutal" (error de sakta hai) str.lower() vs casefold() casefold() = lower() ka "case" wala "full" version — extra aggressive json.dumps vs json.dump Extra "s" = string ke liye. Bina "s" = file ke liye Mutable vs Immutable List, Dict, Set = changeable (LDS = "Large Dynamic Stuff"). String, Tuple, Int = fixed args vs kwargs args = anonymous values (tuple, no name). kwargs = keyword values (dict, has name)

docs.title: 23. Beginner Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
docs.text: Mistake Sahi Tareeqa list2 = list1 (copy samajh kar) list2 = list1.copy() use karo warna dono same object honge Mutable default argument: def f(x=[]): def f(x=None): if x is None: x = [] use karo Bare except: Specific exception catch karo: except ValueError: == ki jagah is use karna values compare karne ke liye == values ke liye, is sirf None/identity ke liye File close() karna bhool jaana Hamesha with open() use karo input() ka result number samajh lena int(input()) ya float(input()) explicitly convert karo Infinite loop (while mein counter update na karna) Loop ke andar counter/condition update karna na bhoolo Indentation errors Consistent 4-space indentation use karo, tabs aur spaces mix mat karo Global variables ka overuse Functions ko parameters aur return values ke through data pass karao print() aur return confuse karna print() sirf dikhata hai, return value deta hai use karne ke liye SQL query mein string formatting (f"SELECT * WHERE name={name}") Parameterized queries use karo (? placeholders) — SQL injection se bachne ke liye Dictionary/list ko loop mein modify karna Copy par loop karo ya naya list/dict banao, original ko iterate karte hue modify mat karo Circular imports Modules ko properly structure karo, imports ko function ke andar move karo agar zaroori ho .format() aur f-strings mix karna inconsistently Ek hi project mein consistent style use karo — modern projects mein f-strings preferred hain

docs.title: 24. Bonus: Extra Topics You Should Also Know
docs.text: Ye kuch aur cheezein hain jo real projects mein bohot common hain aur beginners ko pata honi chahiye:

docs.title: Generators aur yield
docs.text:
def count_up_to(n):
    i = 1
    while i <= n:
        yield i
        i += 1

for num in count_up_to(5):
    print(num)  # 1 2 3 4 5

Generators memory-efficient hote hain — poori list ek sath memory mein nahi rakhte.

docs.title: Context Managers (with)
docs.text: with open() sirf files ke liye nahi — database connections, locks, aur custom resources ke liye bhi use hota hai.

print(now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))  # e.g. 2026-07-30

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text:
def my_decorator(func):
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        print("Before function runs")
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        print("After function runs")
        return result
    return wrapper

@my_decorator
def greet():
    print("Hello!")

greet()

FastAPI/Flask ke @app.get() jaise routes decorators hi hote hain!

docs.title: Type Hints
docs.text:
def add(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return a + b

Type hints code ko readable banate hain aur IDE errors catch karne mein madad karti hain (khaas kar FastAPI/Pydantic mein zaroori hain).

Secrets (API keys, passwords) ko code mein hardcode karne ki bajaye .env file mein rakhna best practice hai.

docs.title: 🎯 Final Note
docs.text:
Ye notes ek reference guide hain — inhe ek baar mein poora yaad karne ki koshish mat karo. Jab bhi kisi project mein koi function/method dikhe jo samajh na aaye, wapas is file mein aakar dhoondo. Practice se hi ye sab dimaag mein permanently set ho jayega.

Best way to learn: Har concept ko chhote se project mein use karke dekho — jaise ek to-do list app, ek simple API, ya ek file organizer script. Real practice se hi confidence aata hai! 🚀
